In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthesis of anthracycline antibiotics.
the production of new anthraquinone and anthracycline compounds from two blocked mutants, ANR-58 and ANR-665, of the aclacinomicyn-producing Streptomyce galilaeus.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 2-hydrosyaklavinone skeleton is formed from the aklavinone skeleton by a hydroxylation reaction, and that the 2-deoxy-aklavinone is formed from the 2-hydoxyaklavinonone skeleton by a dehydroxylation reaction.
the 2-hydoxyaklavinones are biosynthetically formed from anthraquinone precursors.
the 2-hydoxy group is formed by a 1,2-shift from C-1 to C-2 of the 1,2-hydrogen atoms of the anthracyclinon skeleton.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2-hydrxylated compounds are produced from the blocked mutants of Streptomycetes, which produce anthracyclinonoids.
the 7-hydroxyl and the 2-hydrxyl groups in the anthracyclinon skeleton are essential for the biological activity.
the 2-hyroxyl group is introduced in the early stage of the biosynthesis of anthracyclinons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2-hydoxy group is essential for the production of anthracyclinonones.
the 2-hydoxyl group is not necessary for the production of the anthracyclinonones.
the 2-hydrol group is important for the production of the anthracyclinon skeleton.
